metadata.note: The Peoria - Pekin - Havana - Springfield line and the Taylorville Division, as the Chicago & Illinois Midland ran them for passengers 1916-1953, plus three single-year anchors for the line's predecessor operators. Six features, each drawn only for its report's drawable span: C&IM Pekin - Springfield 1926-1953; C&IM Peoria - Pekin over the Peoria & Pekin Union 1926-1932 [OPEN end]; C&IM Taylorville - Auburn 1916-1928 [OPEN both ends]; Springfield & North-Western Springfield - Havana 1875 [ANCHOR]; Peoria, Pekin & Jacksonville Peoria - Havana 1875 [ANCHOR]; Chicago, Peoria & St. Louis Peoria - Springfield 1893 [ANCHOR]. The predecessor features share the C&IM's geometry (Rule 4 splits by operator).
metadata.ownership_split: Springfield - Havana: Springfield & North-Western 1874 (IB&W lease forfeited 1875); Pekin - Havana: Illinois River RR 1859, PP&J 1864, Peoria - Pekin added 1868 (to the P&PU Nov 1880); both Wabash, St. Louis & Pacific 1881 - c.1887 (no drawable Wabash year, not drawn); Chicago, Peoria & St. Louis mid-1888 - 1924; foreclosure 20 Nov 1924 to the Springfield, Havana & Peoria, leased to the C&IM 1926 (the split). NOT splits: the 1936 C&IM - SH&P merger; Commonwealth Edison stock ownership of the C&IM; Peoria entry over the P&PU (trackage rights).
metadata.omitted: Not drawn, per the report's drawable fields: the Pawnee Railroad's Auburn - Pawnee - Pawnee Junction 1889-1906 (no confirmable passenger year); the C&IM's Springfield - Cimic Illinois Central trackage rights and the Compro - Auburn spur (freight only, Jan 1932 Guide). No Wabash-era (1881 - c.1887) feature: the report confirms no passenger year in that operator's era. Havana - Jacksonville (the PP&J's south end) is outside this railroad's scope.
metadata.freight_only_check: Every feature ends with its passenger service or its confirmed year: the whole system was freight-only after 8 May 1953 (now the Illinois & Midland, G&W); Peoria - Pekin freight-only after the 1932-1944 cutback (Feb 1952 Guide Note A); Taylorville Division freight-only by Jan 1932; Springfield - Cimic and Compro - Auburn freight-only and excluded.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: 1. [OPEN] cim-peoria-pekin ends 1932: the cutback to Pekin falls between 1932 and 1944 (Fowler 1944G terminus), undated. 2. [OPEN] cim-taylorville-auburn is drawn 1916-1928: start bracket c.1906-1916, end bracket 1928-1932. 3. [ANCHOR] snw-springfield-havana 1875 and ppj-peoria-havana 1875; [ANCHOR] cpstl-peoria-springfield 1893 - the whole 1874-1926 predecessor era, including the Wabash years 1881 - c.1887 and 1894-1926, is otherwise unproven; CP&StL is not in research/QUEUE.tsv and needs its own pass. 4. cim-pekin-springfield's 1953 end rests on one secondary source (American-Rails) - a May 1953 newspaper item would settle it; the late-1940s cut to one train is undated. 5. Which Springfield station the C&IM used, and which P&PU line (east or west bank) its Peoria trains took, are not established. 6. Whether the IB&W or the S&NW ran the 1875 Springfield - Havana trains.
metadata.conflicts: Last train: American-Rails 8 May 1953 vs a possible 1954 reading of Passenger Train Journal; 1953 used. Guide scan date: headed 13 Jan 1932, captioned Mar 1933 edition; 1932 used. Peoria - Pekin route: Fowler 'P&PU (Western)' vs the Guide's 9.3 mi, which fits the east-bank P&PU line (9.5 mi traced) and not the west-bank one (13.0 mi); east bank drawn.

properties.line: Chicago and Illinois Midland: Pekin – Springfield
properties.speed_source: ESTIMATE from the Jan 1932 Official Guide: train 7 Peoria 3:15 PM - Springfield 6:36 PM, 87.1 mi in 3 h 21 min (about 42 km/h) with all stops; other years not timed
geometry_source: OpenStreetMap ways tagged old_railway_operator=C&IM (today's Illinois and Midland Railroad, active, disused and razed), routed with opstrace.py via the Overpass mirror maps.mail.ru, traced 2026-10-31
properties.geometry_quality: Real-traced, no straight-line legs: 77.1 mi Pekin - Springfield against 77.8 mi documented (Jan 1932 Official Guide: Pekin 9.3, Springfield 87.1 from Peoria; Fowler 10.2 - 88.0). 77.0 mi on track tagged old_railway_operator=C&IM (today the Illinois & Midland, G&W), 0.2 mi untagged. Every waypoint (Pekin, Manito, Forest City, Havana, Kilbourne, Oakford, Petersburg, Athens, Cantrall) lies within 0.3 km of the line; measured from Peoria, Havana lands at 39.9 mi (Fowler 41.0) and the Springfield end at 86.6 (Guide 87.1). Springfield end: the south end of the C&IM-tagged track near 15th St (39.801 N); which Springfield station the trains used (the C&IM's own, or Union Station, 1.5 mi past Shops) is not established. LATER ALIGNMENT: this is the line as OSM records it today; any relocations made during the C&IM's freight years after 1953 are not backed out - none is known to the research.

segments.note: The Springfield, Havana & Peoria Railroad bought the line at the Chicago, Peoria & St. Louis foreclosure (20 Nov 1924; ICC certificate 13 Feb 1926) and leased it to the Chicago & Illinois Midland in 1926; merged into the C&IM 1936, which did not change who ran the trains (not a split). 1926: two daily round trips Springfield - Peoria (American-Rails). Jan 1932 Official Guide: trains 5/7 southbound and 6/8 northbound, all daily, Peoria - Pekin - Havana - Springfield, about 3 h 21 min end to end. Reduced to one weekday round trip in the late 1940s (American-Rails; year not dated, so not split here); the Feb 1952 Guide still prints the table with a 'Daily, except Sunday' legend but no times survive in the OCR. Steam to the end (4-4-0s 500-502). Last passenger train 8 May 1953, at Kilbourne (American-Rails, with a dated crew photo). CONFLICT, recorded: Passenger Train Journal, beside a Dec 1954 photo of a club special at Peoria, writes of the regular run in a way that could be read as still running in 1954; the 1953 end is used. The 1926 start is the lease year; the exact first C&IM train date was not found. Freight continued; the line is the Illinois & Midland (Genesee & Wyoming) today. Headway: two trains each way 1926 - late 1940s; one each way on weekdays after that - the 720 figure is an estimate from the train counts.
sources: Segment-level: start (1926 lease, two daily round trips) from American-Rails; 1932 service with times from the Jan 1932 Official Guide p.409; end (last train 8 May 1953) from American-Rails, with the Passenger Train Journal 1954 reading recorded as a conflict. Headway estimated from train counts.

properties.line: Chicago and Illinois Midland: Peoria – Pekin (via P&PU)
properties.speed_source: ESTIMATE: the through-train average from the Jan 1932 Official Guide (87.1 mi Peoria - Springfield in 3 h 21 min); the Peoria - Pekin leg was not timed separately
geometry_source: OpenStreetMap untagged active railway (no operator or old_railway_operator tag) between Peoria and Pekin, routed with opstrace.py via the Overpass mirror maps.mail.ru, traced 2026-10-31
properties.geometry_quality: Peoria - Pekin 9.5 mi against 9.3 mi documented (Jan 1932 Official Guide: Pekin 9.3 from Peoria). Real-traced, no straight-line legs, all 9.5 mi on OSM track with no operator tag: from the downtown Peoria riverfront (the Union Depot site, approximated by the Peoria city geocode, 0.5 km off the line) south-west along the river, across the Illinois River at about 40.667 N, then down the EAST bank past Creve Coeur into Pekin. WHOSE TRACK: this is the Peoria & Pekin Union's east-bank line as OSM records it today (untagged); the C&IM ran over P&PU track by trackage rights. CONFLICT, recorded: Fowler says the C&IM 'operated via Peoria & Pekin Union (Western)', and the west-bank line (UP Peoria Subdivision, ex-C&NW, via Bartonville, crossing the river south-west of Pekin and joining the C&IM there) was traced too, but it measures 13.0 mi Peoria - Pekin station, 40% over the Guide's 9.3; the east-bank route measures 9.5. The mileage is the reason the east bank is drawn - which P&PU line the trains actually used is NOT established. The Peoria terminal approach is the modern track layout, not the 1926-32 Union Depot trackage.

segments.note: The C&IM's through Peoria - Springfield trains over the Peoria & Pekin Union by trackage rights; the C&IM owned nothing north of Pekin (American-Rails). Not an ownership split - the same C&IM trains as the Pekin - Springfield feature. Peoria is the timetable origin, with times, in the Jan 1932 Official Guide (trains 7 and 5 from Peoria 3:15 PM and 7:00 AM daily). [OPEN] end: 1932 is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known ending. The trains were cut back to Pekin some time between 1932 and 1944 - Fowler marks Pekin the terminus of service in the 1944 Guide, and the Feb 1952 Guide's Note A reads 'Freight service only is available between Peoria and Pekin' - but no source dates the cutback. Do not extend without evidence. The Guide scan is headed 13 Jan 1932 though American-Rails captions it as the Mar 1933 edition; the earlier year is used. The Dec 1954 C&IM-coach special at Peoria Union Depot (Passenger Train Journal) was a one-off club extra, not drawn. Headway as on the main line, an estimate from the 1932 train count.
sources: Segment-level: 1926 through trains from American-Rails; Peoria with times in the Jan 1932 Official Guide; cutback bracket from Fowler table 190 (Pekin 1944G terminus) and the Feb 1952 Guide Note A. End year is the last confirmed, not a known end. Headway estimated.

properties.geometry_quality: Real-traced, no straight-line legs: 24.2 mi Taylorville - Auburn against 24.2 mi in the Jan 1932 Official Guide (Auburn 4.2 - Taylorville 28.4 from Compro) and 25.2 mi in Fowler table 191. 23.7 mi on C&IM-tagged ways and 0.6 mi untagged at the Taylorville end. WHOSE TRACK: Auburn - Cimic is a lifted grade mapped in OSM as razed (old_railway_operator=C&IM); Cimic - Kincaid area is active Illinois & Midland track; east of about 89.44 W to Taylorville the track is tagged disused (out of service but in place). The Taylorville end stops about 1.2 km from the town centre where the traced track ends; the C&IM depot's exact site is not established. The Auburn end is Auburn itself; the Compro - Auburn spur to the Chicago & Alton (freight only in the 1932 Guide) is not drawn. LATER ALIGNMENT: the line as OSM records it, not checked against a 1916-28 map.

segments.note: The C&IM's Taylorville Division: the Pawnee Railroad's Auburn - Pawnee - Pawnee Junction (Cimic, Illinois Central crossing) line, run by C&IM forces from 1 Feb 1906, plus the C&IM's own Pawnee - Kincaid - Taylorville extension (reportedly 1906, unverified); a coal road serving Commonwealth Edison's mines. Fowler's station letters show passenger stations Taylorville - Auburn in the 1916 Official Guide and a 1928 company public timetable (Bulpitt and Beechley in 1916 only). [OPEN] at both ends: 1916 is the first and 1928 the last CONFIRMED year, not known dates. Service may have begun with the 1906 extension and ended as late as 1931 - by the Jan 1932 Guide the line is printed 'Freight service only' - but no source in hand proves any year outside 1916-1928. Do not extend without evidence. Whether the trains ran through to Springfield over the Illinois Central (C&IM trackage rights Springfield - Cimic, freight only in 1932) is unknown; that link is not drawn. Fowler's 'Cimic 1930G' is not used (name change or service, unclear). Consist (local or mixed) and frequency unknown: the headway is a guess. Freight continued; Cimic - Taylorville is now out of service, Cimic - Auburn lifted.
sources: Segment-level: Fowler table 191 station letters (a: 1916 Official Guide; b: 1928 company timetable); the Jan 1932 Official Guide prints the line freight-only. Start and end are confirmed years, not known dates. Headway NOT SOURCED.

LATER ALIGNMENT: this draws the C&IM-era line as OSM records it today, not the 1874 S&NW alignment; no source says whether the road was relocated in between. The Springfield end is the C&IM's (south end of the C&IM-tagged track near 15th St); the S&NW's own 1875 Springfield terminus is not established.

segments.note: The Springfield & North-Western, completed Springfield - Havana in Dec 1874; trains reached Peoria over the Peoria, Pekin & Jacksonville via Havana (Wikipedia, CP&StL). Leased to the Indianapolis, Bloomington & Western until the lease was forfeited in 1875 - which company actually ran the 1875 trains is therefore not settled; the line is drawn under the S&NW, its owner and the operator after the forfeiture. Wabash, St. Louis & Pacific operation began only in 1881, so this is not a Wabash feature. Fowler's 'y' letter (1875 Official Guide) is on Havana, Kilbourne, Oakford, Atterberry, Petersburg, Tice, Athens, Cantrall and Springfield. [ANCHOR]: 1875 is the one proven year. Service certainly ran wider both ways - from Dec 1874 and on under the Wabash (1881 - c.1887) and the Chicago, Peoria & St. Louis (1888 on) - but no other year in this operator's era is confirmed. Do not widen without evidence. Headway is a guess, not sourced.

properties.geometry_quality: Real-traced, no straight-line legs: 39.9 mi Peoria - Havana against about 41 mi documented (Fowler table 190, 0 - 41.0). Peoria - Pekin (9.5 mi) is the same east-bank P&PU trace as the C&IM's Peoria - Pekin feature - see the conflict recorded there (Fowler's 'P&PU (Western)' vs the 9.3 mi Guide mileage); Pekin - Havana (30.4 mi) is cut from the C&IM trace, all on C&IM-tagged track. LATER ALIGNMENT: the whole feature draws the line as OSM records it today. Peoria - Pekin in 1875 was the PP&J's own track, which passed to the Peoria & Pekin Union only in Nov 1880; whether the P&PU kept, relocated or replaced it - and so whether the 1875 line is the east-bank route drawn here - is not established. The Peoria terminal is the modern riverfront layout, approximated at the Peoria geocode (0.5 km off the line).

segments.note: The north end of the Peoria, Pekin & Jacksonville's Jacksonville - Havana - Pekin - Peoria line (Pekin - Havana opened 1859 by the Illinois River Railroad; PP&J from 1864; Peoria - Pekin bought by the PP&J May 1868; Wabash operation only from 1881, so not a Wabash feature). Havana - Jacksonville (later the Jacksonville & Havana) is outside this layer's scope and not drawn. Fowler's 'y' letter (1875 Official Guide) is on Peoria, Pekin, Gravel Bluff, Manito, Forest City, Bishop's, Topeka and Havana. [ANCHOR]: 1875 is the one proven year. Service certainly ran wider - the 1859 and 1868 openings are secondary-sourced corporate dates, not passenger evidence, and trains continued under the Wabash and the CP&StL - but no other PP&J year is confirmed. Do not widen without evidence. Headway is a guess, not sourced.

segments.note: The Chicago, Peoria & St. Louis, which bought the Springfield - Havana - Pekin - Peoria line in mid-1888 (Wikipedia, CP&StL); part of the Jacksonville Southeastern system 1890-1893; later reorganised as the CP&StL Railroad of Illinois (1896), Railway of Illinois (1900) and Railroad (1913-1924) - the same road, not splits. Fowler's 'z' letter (1893 Official Guide) is on Quiver, Bishop's, Hainesville and Cora. [ANCHOR]: 1893 is the one proven year in the CP&StL era. Service certainly ran wider (1888 to the 1924 foreclosure, at least), but nothing else is confirmed in hand; Fowler's own 'pass?' 1922 notices are not used, and whether receivers or the Springfield, Havana & Peoria ran trains 1924-1926 is unknown. Do not widen without evidence - a dedicated CP&StL research pass is recommended. Headway is a guess, not sourced.
